source_attestations.note: Ashnod the Uncaring — RULES PASS WITH DOCUMENTATION CORRECTION

summary:
Ashnod the Uncaring copies every non-mana artifact or creature ability that sacrificed a permanent to activate. The source's correction (no once-per-turn limit, tokens count) is re-verified against current Oracle.

Bot cycle 48: the combo lines are now checked against cached Commander Spellbook steps, which corrected this review's earlier claim that the Scrap Trawler + Myr Retriever loop needs a simultaneous sacrifice (see ashnod-08). The list is unchanged; documentation flags record the stale source wording and the corrected entry.

interactions.title: Current Oracle: no once-per-turn limit, tokens count
interactions.ruling: Ashnod copies any non-mana activated ability of an artifact or creature whose cost included sacrificing one or more permanents. The copy is free and may get new targets. There is no once-per-turn limit. The sacrificed permanent can be a token (Clue, Treasure, Servo). The source repo's older notes assumed a once-per-turn, nontoken version; the retrospective corrected that.
interactions.short: Copies every non-mana artifact/creature ability that sacrificed something to activate; no turn limit, tokens count.

flag.note: The source's older Ashnod notes describe a once-per-turn, nontoken restriction that current Oracle doesn't have. The retrospective and Ashnod_Oracle_Correction_2026-10-14.md already repair it; noted so older source text isn't reused.

oracle.quote: Whenever you activate an ability of an artifact or creature that isn't a mana ability, if one or more permanents were sacrificed to activate it, you may copy that ability.

source.quote: Current Ashnod has **no once-per-turn restriction** and does **not** require the sacrificed permanent to be nontoken.

interactions.title: Mana abilities and resolution-time sacrifices don't count
interactions.ruling: Ashnod's Altar, Krark-Clan Ironworks, Lotus Petal and Treasures are mana abilities, so they're never copied. Sacrificing a Treasure *for the mana* to pay a cost doesn't count either. Goblin Welder's sacrifice happens on resolution, not as a cost, so Ashnod doesn't copy it.

oracle.quote: (Sacrificing an artifact for mana to activate an ability doesn't count.)

rulings.quote: Sacrificing an artifact, such as a Treasure token, to create mana that you used to pay an activation cost doesn’t count.

source.quote: the prior `Goblin Welder` noninteraction conclusion therefore remains correct.

interactions.title: Sacrifice-cost artifacts become two-for-one
interactions.ruling:
Each of these sacrifices itself (or another permanent) as a cost, so Ashnod copies the ability:
- Bauble: two delayed draws.
- Wayfarer's Bauble: two basic lands.
- Moonsilver Key: two tutors.
- Executioner's Capsule and Pyrite Spellbomb: a second target.
- Mind Stone, Mnemonic Sphere, Skullbomb, Dockside Chef: extra cards.

The copy keeps the original's targets unless you change them.
interactions.short: Self-sacrificing artifacts give double value with Ashnod.

oracle.quote: {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Look at the top card of target player's library. Draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep.

interactions.title: Time Sieve copied: two extra turns
interactions.ruling: Time Sieve's ability sacrifices five artifacts (it can be one of them), so Ashnod copies it: you take two extra turns. If Time Sieve itself was sacrificed, the copy still resolves. Abilities exist independently of their source.

oracle.quote: {T}, Sacrifice five artifacts: Take an extra turn after this one.

rulings.quote: You may sacrifice Time Sieve as one of the artifacts to pay the cost of its own ability.

source.quote: `Oni-Cult Anvil`, `Arcbound Ravager`, `Trading Post` sacrifice modes, `Repurposing Bay`, `Time Sieve`, and other nonmana artifact/creature activated abilities qualify

interactions.title: Copies use the original's sacrificed-object information
interactions.ruling: A copied ability copies the decisions made for it, including costs paid. The copy of Repurposing Bay looks for MV 1 + the sacrificed artifact's MV, and the copy of Altar of Dementia mills equal to the sacrificed creature's power, without a new sacrifice. Kuldotha Forgemaster's copy fetches a second artifact. A mana value with X counts X as 0.

oracle.quote: Search your library for an artifact card with mana value equal to 1 plus the sacrificed artifact's mana value

rulings.quote: If there’s an {X} in the sacrificed artifact’s mana cost, X is 0 when determining its mana value.

interactions.title: Rings of Brighthearth and Ashnod both copy
interactions.ruling: Rings ({2} for any non-mana ability) and Ashnod trigger separately on the same activation, and you order the triggers. Each makes one copy. Copies aren't activated, so they don't retrigger either card. If Rings was sacrificed to pay the cost, its trigger doesn't happen.

oracle.quote: Whenever you activate an ability, if it isn't a mana ability, you may pay {2}. If you do, copy that ability.

rulings.quote: If paying the activation cost of the ability includes sacrificing Rings of Brighthearth, the ability won't be copied.

interactions.title: Clan Crafter on Ashnod
interactions.ruling: Clan Crafter is a Background in the 99, cast as a normal enchantment. Ashnod has no Choose a Background, so it isn't a second commander. It gives commander creatures you own '{2}, Sacrifice an artifact: +1/+1 counter and draw'. That's an activated ability of a creature with a sacrifice cost, so Ashnod copies it: two counters, two cards.

oracle.quote: Commander creatures you own have "{2}, Sacrifice an artifact: Put a +1/+1 counter on this creature and draw a card."

interactions.title: Scrap Trawler + Myr Retriever + Altar or KCI + a cost reducer
interactions.ruling:
Spellbook's line (for example 1020-1976-2034-2866, cached) is *sequential*. It starts with one artifact creature on the battlefield and the other in the graveyard:
1. Sacrifice Myr Retriever for {C}{C}; its trigger returns Scrap Trawler to hand. Cast Trawler (reduced).
2. Sacrifice Trawler for {C}{C}; its own death trigger returns Retriever (MV 2 < 3). Cast Retriever (reduced).

With one reducer, the two casts cost 3 and the two sacrifices give 4, so each loop nets {C}. The Sai and Crime Novelist variants replace the reducer with Thopter fodder or {R}.

Correction: the batch-A version of this entry said both had to be sacrificed during one cost payment. That was wrong. It started from both on the battlefield; Spellbook's starting position avoids that.
interactions.short: Spellbook infinite: alternate Retriever and Trawler through an altar; a reducer makes it mana-positive.

flag.note: Corrects this review's own batch-A wording (Bot cycle 46), which said the loop needed a simultaneous sacrifice. Spellbook's sequential line, starting with one creature in the graveyard, is simpler and is now the recorded line. No list change.

oracle.quote: Whenever this creature dies or another artifact you control is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, return to your hand target artifact card in your graveyard with lesser mana value.
When this creature dies, return another target artifact card from your graveyard to your hand.

spellbook.quote: When Scrap Trawler dies, it triggers, returning Myr Retriever from your graveyard to your hand.
One of the artifact creatures must be on the battlefield, with the other in your graveyard.

interactions.title: Nim Deathmantle loops (Apprentice, Urza, Farid)
interactions.ruling:
Spellbook's lines (cached) all pay {4} to Nim Deathmantle from altar mana. The Altar is a mana ability, so Ashnod doesn't copy it.
- **Marionette Apprentice (2034-5003-6199):** sacrifice Apprentice ({C}{C}), return it with Deathmantle, sacrifice the Servo from its fabricate ({C}{C}). Each death drains opponents.
- **Urza (457-2034-5003):** sacrifice Urza and the Construct its enter trigger makes.
- **Farid with KCI (4659-5003-5272):** sacrifice a nontoken artifact creature, then the Scrap token from Farid, then pay Deathmantle's {4}.

oracle.quote: Whenever a nontoken creature is put into your graveyard from the battlefield, you may pay {4}. If you do, return that card to the battlefield and attach this Equipment to it.

spellbook.quote: When Marionette Apprentice dies, Nim Deathmantle triggers, causing you to pay {4} to return Marionette Apprentice from your graveyard to the battlefield and attach Nim Deathmantle to it.
Resolve the Farid trigger, creating a Scrap artifact token.

interactions.title: Dross Scorpion + Retrofitter Foundry + Altar or KCI
interactions.ruling: Retrofitter Foundry makes a Servo for {2}, {T}. Sacrificing that Servo (an artifact creature) to the Altar gives {C}{C}, and Dross Scorpion untaps Foundry. Repeating this is mana-neutral and gives unlimited death and enter/leave triggers (Marionette Apprentice, Disciple of the Vault drains). Foundry's Thopter and Construct modes sacrifice tokens to activate, so Ashnod copies those (a second Thopter or Construct).
interactions.short: Spellbook infinite: Foundry Servo, Altar sacrifice, Scorpion untap.

oracle.quote: Whenever this creature or another artifact creature dies, you may untap target artifact.
{2}, {T}: Create a 1/1 colorless Servo artifact creature token.

interactions.title: Leave-the-battlefield payoffs
interactions.ruling:
- **Oni-Cult Anvil:** its {T}, sacrifice ability is copied by Ashnod. Its Construct trigger happens once per turn, on your turn only.
- **Disciple of the Vault and Marionette Apprentice:** trigger on artifacts (tokens included) going to the graveyard.
- **Mayhem Devil:** pings on every sacrifice by any player.
- **Esoteric Duplicator:** offers a {2} end-step copy of each sacrificed artifact.

oracle.quote: This ability triggers only once each turn.

interactions.title: Commander tax and Ashnod's deathtouch
interactions.ruling: Ashnod costs {2}{U}{B}{R}, then 7, then 9. Deathtouch applies only to damage Ashnod deals itself. Blasting Station's and Walking Ballista's pings come from those sources. Walking Ballista's counter removal isn't a sacrifice, so Ashnod doesn't copy it. Blasting Station's sacrifice ability is copied (an extra point of damage).

oracle.quote: {T}, Sacrifice a creature: This artifact deals 1 damage to any target.
